Name of the Surah

• It is called al-Mu'minun (The Believers), because it opens with mention of the believers and their success, and because it contains their sublime qualities and their reward in the Hereafter.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• Giving glad tidings to the believers of a great success, because of their adornment with the foundations of spiritual and practical virtues, through which the soul is purified, conduct is made upright, and they become worthy of inheriting the highest Paradise (al-Firdaws al-A'la) in the Gardens of Eternity.

• Clarifying the proofs of God's Oneness in the creation of man, plants and animals, and reminding man of the stages through which he passed in his creation, and the indication of that for proving resurrection after death, and that God did not create creation in vain (sudan).

• Affirming the unity of the messages, and reminding of the sending of the Messengers to guide to Tawhid (Monotheism) and righteous action, and the rejection their peoples met them with, and the punishment of those who denied them; as a reminder and admonition to those who turn away from the call of the Prophet (ﷺ), and as consolation to him for the harm and denial and mockery he suffered from the polytheists.

• Teaching the Prophet (ﷺ) some of the legal etiquettes in supplication, in responding to enemies, and in seeking refuge with God, glorified and exalted is He.

• Mention of what occurs after death of the scenes of the Resurrection: the gathering and the raising up, the division of people into two groups, so that neither lineage nor ancestry will benefit anyone on that Day; only righteous deeds will avail. Also mention of the state of the people of misery and where they end up, and the state of the people of happiness at the announcement of their victory in the Hereafter.

[Tafsir]

The believers who affirm God and His Messenger and act according to His law have indeed succeeded.
Those who, among their qualities, are humbly focused (khushu') in their prayer: their hearts are emptied for it, and their limbs are calm.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 3:

﴿And those who turn away from all that is vain and useless in speech and deeds.﴾

The commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 4:

And those who purify their souls and their wealth by paying the zakat (obligatory almsgiving) on their wealth, across its various kinds.
Those who guard their private parts from what Allah has forbidden, such as fornication, sodomy, and all other immoral acts.

Except with their wives or what their right hands possess of slave-women, for then they are not blameworthy, and there is no sin upon them in having intercourse with them and enjoying them, because Allah the Most High has made them lawful.

Whoever seeks sexual gratification other than with his wife or his slave-woman has transgressed from what is lawful to what is unlawful, and he has exposed himself to the punishment and wrath of Allah.
And those who are faithful guardians of everything entrusted to them, and who fulfill all their covenants.
And those who are constant in performing their prayers at their appointed times, in the manner prescribed for them, as transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ).
These believers are the inheritors of Paradise.
The ones who inherit the highest ranks of Paradise and its middle part, and these are its most excellent abode; they will abide therein forever, their bliss never ceasing nor passing away.
We have certainly created Adam from clay, taken from all of the earth.
Then We created his offspring, generating one from another, from a drop: the semen of men, which issues from their loins and settles firmly in the wombs of women.

Then We made the drop into a clinging clot (ʿalaqah), that is, red blood. Then We made the clot into a lump of flesh (muḍghah), that is, a piece of flesh the size of what can be chewed. Then We made the lump into bones, and clothed the bones with flesh. Then We brought it into being as another creation by breathing the spirit into it. So blessed is Allah, the Best of Creators.
Then, indeed, you human beings, after the stages of life and the expiry of your lifespans, are surely going to die.
Then, after death and the ending of this worldly life, you will be raised up from your graves on the Day of Resurrection for reckoning and recompense.
And We have certainly created above you seven heavens, one above another, and We have never been unaware of creation; so We do not neglect any creature, nor do We forget it.

We sent down water from the sky in measure suited to the needs of creation, and We made the earth a resting place for this water. Indeed, We are able to take the stored water away. In this there is a warning and threat for the wrongdoers.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 19:

So We brought forth for you, by this water, gardens of date palms and grapevines. In them you have many kinds of fruit of varied types and shapes, and from them you eat.
And We brought forth for you, by means of it, the olive tree that grows around Mount Tur (Sinai). From it oil is pressed, with which people anoint themselves and use it as a condiment.

And indeed, for you, O people, in the camels, the cattle, and the sheep, there is a lesson for you to reflect upon through their creation. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies of milk. And for you in them are many other benefits, such as wool, hides, and the like, and from them you eat.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 23, verse 22:

And upon the camels and the ships, on land and at sea, you are carried.

And We certainly sent Noah to his people, calling them to monotheism. He said to them: "Worship Allah alone; you have no deity worthy of worship other than Him, exalted is He. So devote your worship sincerely to Him. Will you not fear His punishment?"

The chieftains of his people, who disbelieved, said to their common folk: "He is only a human being like you, who has no distinction over you in anything. He desires by his words nothing but leadership and superiority over you. Had God willed to send a messenger, He would have sent angels. We never heard of such a thing among our fathers and forefathers of old. He is only a man possessed by madness, so wait for him until he recovers, [and then] he will abandon his call, or he will die, and you will be rid of him."

The chieftains of his people, who disbelieved, said to their common folk: "He is only a human being like you, who has no distinction over you in anything. He desires by his words nothing but leadership and superiority over you. Had God willed to send a messenger, He would have sent angels. We never heard of such a thing among our fathers and forefathers of old. He is only a man possessed by madness, so wait for him until he recovers, [and then] he will abandon his call, or he will die, and you will be rid of him."
Noah said: "My Lord, support me against my people, because of their denial of me in what I conveyed to them of Your message."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 27:

So We revealed to him: "Build the ship under Our eyes and by Our command. When Our command comes and the punishment of your people by drowning is due, and the flood begins, the water will gush forth powerfully from the tannur (the oven, the place where bread is baked) as a sign of the coming of the punishment. Then load into the ship pairs of every living creature, male and female, so that the offspring may survive. And take aboard your family, except those who deserve the punishment because of their disbelief, such as your wife and your son. Do not ask Me to save your people who wronged themselves, for they are surely going to be drowned."

﴿فأوحينا إليه أن اصنع السفينة بمرأى منا وبأمرنا﴾ — "So We revealed to him: Build the ship under Our eyes and by Our command."

And in this verse is the affirmation of the attribute of the Eye for Allah, the Exalted, in a manner befitting Him, without likening Him to anything and without asking how.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 28:

"Then when you and those with you have settled in the ship, safe from drowning, say: Praise be to God, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 29:

Say: "My Lord, cause me to land at a blessed landing place, and You are the best of those who bring to land." And in this is a teaching from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His servants: when they alight, they should say this supplication.

In the rescue of the believers and the destruction of the disbelievers there are clear signs confirming the truthfulness of God's messengers in what they brought from God, and indeed We were testing the nations by sending the messengers to them before punishment befell them.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 23, verse 31:**

Then We brought into being, after the people of Noah, another generation: they are the people of ʿAd.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 32:

So We sent among them a messenger from among themselves, Hud (peace be upon him), and he said to them: "Worship Allah alone; you have no deity worthy of worship besides Him. Will you not then fear His punishment if you worship other than Him?"

The eminent and notables of his people, who disbelieved in God and denied the Hereafter, and whom the luxury of worldly life that had been bestowed upon them had made arrogant, said: "This is no more than a human being like you, who eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink, and who calls you to the Oneness of God Most High."

This is the commentary on Surah al-Mu'minun (23), verse 34, as given in al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the King Fahd Complex tafsir):

"And if you obey a man like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers, by abandoning your gods and following him."
How can you believe what he promises you: that when you die, and become dust and crumbling bones, you will be brought out of your graves alive?

The commentary on surah 23, verse 36:

"Far-fetched indeed is what you are promised, O people: that after your death you will be brought out alive from your graves."
There is no life but our life in this world: some of us die and others live, and we will never be brought forth alive again.
This one who calls you to belief is only a man who has invented a lie against God, and we will not believe what he has told us.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 39:

So their messenger called upon his Lord, saying: "My Lord, help me against them, because they have denied me."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 40:

God said in answer to his supplication: "In a little while they will surely become regretful." That is, after a short time these deniers will become regretful.

And not long after, a mighty blast seized them, together with a wind, by which Allah destroyed them. So they all died, and they became like the refuse of the flood that floats upon the water. So destruction to these wrongdoers, and far removed are they from the mercy of Allah. Let those who hear beware of denying their Messenger, lest there befall them what befell those before them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 42:

Then We brought into being, after those deniers, other nations and creatures, such as the peoples of Lot, Shu'ayb, Ayyub and Yunus, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all.
No nation from these deniing peoples advances beyond the appointed time set for its destruction, nor does it fall behind it.

Then We sent Our messengers to those nations, one after another. Every time a messenger came to his community, they denied him. So We made them follow one another into destruction and ruin, and nothing remained of them but the reports of their destruction. We made them into tales for those who came after them, that they might take them as a lesson. So destruction and ruin upon a people who do not believe the messengers and do not obey them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verses 45–46:

Then We sent Musa (Moses) and his brother Harun (Aaron) with Our signs and a clear authority, namely the nine signs: the staff, the hand, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the flood, the years of drought, and the loss of fruits, a clear proof that overpowers hearts, so that the hearts of the believers submit to it, and the proof is established against the obstinate. We sent them both to Fir'awn (Pharaoh), the ruler of "Misr" (Egypt), and to the nobles of his people. But they were arrogant and refused to believe in Musa and his brother, for they were a people who acted haughtily over others and dominated them through injustice.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verses 45–46:

Then We sent Musa (Moses) and his brother Harun (Aaron) with Our signs and a clear authority, namely the nine signs: the staff, the hand, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the flood, the years of drought, and the loss of fruits, a clear proof that overpowers hearts, so that the hearts of the believers submit to it, and the proof is established against the obstinate. We sent them both to Fir'awn (Pharaoh), the ruler of "Misr" (Egypt), and to the nobles of his people. But they were arrogant and refused to believe in Musa and his brother, for they were a people who acted haughtily over others and dominated them through injustice.
So they said: "Shall we believe two men like ourselves, when their people, the Children of Israel, are under our authority, obedient and submissive to us?"
So they denied the two of them in what they brought, and so they were among those destroyed by drowning in the sea.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 49:

And We indeed gave Moses the Torah, so that his people might be guided by it to the truth.

And We made ʿĪsā (Jesus), son of Maryam (Mary), and his mother a sign, evidence of Our power, since We created him without a father. And We gave them both a shelter on a raised piece of land, level enough to settle upon, with fertile soil and flowing water visible to the eyes.

O Messengers, eat of the good and lawful provisions, and do righteous deeds. Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do; nothing of your deeds is hidden from Me.

The address in the verse is general, to the Messengers (peace be upon them) and their followers. The verse is evidence that eating what is lawful helps one to do righteous deeds, and that the consequence of what is unlawful is grave, among which is that one's supplication is rejected.
Indeed, your religion, O messengers, is one religion, which is Islam. I am your Lord, so fear Me by carrying out My commands and avoiding My prohibitions.

So the followers split into factions and sects in their religion; they made their religion into many religions after they had been commanded to unite. Each faction is pleased with its own opinion, claiming that it is upon the truth and that others are upon falsehood. In this there is a warning against partisanship and division in religion.
So leave them, O Messenger, in their error and their ignorance of the truth, until the punishment descends upon them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verses 55–56:

Do these disbelievers think that what We extend to them of wealth and children in this world is a hastening of good for them that they deserve? Rather, We hasten good for them as a trial for them and a gradual leading-on (*istidraj*), but they do not perceive that.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verses 55–56:

Do these disbelievers think that what We extend to them of wealth and children in this world is a hastening of good for them that they deserve? Rather, We hasten good for them as a trial for them and a gradual leading-on (*istidraj*), but they do not perceive that.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 57:

Indeed, those who are fearful of their Lord's displeasure, apprehensive and anxious about what Allah the Exalted has warned them of.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 58:

And those who believe in the signs of Allah in the Qur'an, and act upon them.
Those who devote their worship to Allah alone, and do not associate anything with Him.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 23, verse 60:

And those who strive hard in doing good deeds and acts of righteousness, while their hearts are fearful that their deeds will not be accepted, and that they will not be saved from the punishment of their Lord when they return to Him for reckoning.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 61:

Those are the ones who strive hard in obedience; their habit is to hasten to every righteous deed, and they are foremost in doing good.

We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity, and their deeds are recorded with Us in a Book that records every deed, which the angels raise up; it speaks the truth against them, and none of them will be wronged.

But the hearts of the disbelievers are in thorough heedlessness of this Qur'an and what it contains. Besides their polytheism, they have evil deeds, which Allah lets them carry on so that they may incur His wrath and punishment.
Until, when We seize the affluent among them, those lost in pride and excess, with Our punishment, they suddenly raise their voices, pleading humbly and crying out for help.
It will be said to them: "Do not cry out or call for help today. Indeed, you cannot help yourselves, and no one can protect you from the punishment of God."

This is the commentary on Q. 23:66 (al-Mu'minun), and the translation follows.

"Indeed, My verses were being recited to you, [so that you would believe in them], but you used to turn back on your heels (in aversion) when hearing them, and [you would refuse] to accept them as true and act upon them, like one who turns back on his heels by retreating backward."

You act this way, arrogant toward people without right, because of the Sacred House of God, saying, "We are its people, and we will not be overcome in it," and you spend your evenings around it talking about evil.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "the Simplified Tafsir") on surah 23, verse 68:**

Have they not then pondered over the Qur'an, so that they would recognize its truthfulness? Or has something prevented them from believing, namely that there came to them a messenger and a Book that had not come to their forefathers of old, so that they denied it and turned away from it?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 69:

Or has it been that their Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), is unknown to them, so that they deny him?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 70:

Or do they say, "He is possessed"? Rather, he has brought them the truth, and most of them are averse to the truth out of envy and insolence.

If Allah had legislated for them what matches their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted. Rather, We brought them that which contains their honour and nobility, namely the Qur'an, yet they turn away from it.

Or do you ask them for a payment, O Messenger, which is why they refuse? No, you do not ask them for anything. What is with your Lord of reward and bounty is better, and He is the best of providers. No one can provide the like of His provision, glory be to Him and exalted is He.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 73:

And indeed you, O Messenger, call your people and others to a straight religion, which is the religion of Islam.
Indeed, those who do not believe in the resurrection and the reckoning, and do not act for them, are deviating from the straight religion toward something other than it.
Even if We had shown them mercy and removed from them the famine and hunger they were suffering, they would have persisted in disbelief and obstinacy, wandering in bewilderment and confusion.
And We had already tested them with various kinds of calamities, yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they implore Him with humility when those calamities came upon them.
﴿Until, when We open for them a gate of severe punishment in the Hereafter, they will be in despair of every good, bewildered, not knowing what to do.﴾

And He it is Who brought into being for you hearing, to perceive what is heard, and sight, to perceive what is seen, and hearts, so that you might understand thereby. Yet your gratitude for these successive blessings bestowed upon you is little, hardly worth mentioning.
And it is He who created all of mankind on the earth, and to Him you will be gathered after your death, so that He may recompense you for what you have done of good or evil.

He is the One who gives life from non-existence and causes death after life. The alternation of night and day, and their differing lengths, belong to Him alone. Will you not then reflect on His power and His oneness?
"But the disbelievers did not believe in the resurrection; rather, they repeated the saying of their forebears who denied it."
They said: "When we die and our bodies and bones have decayed into the dust of the earth, will we be brought back to life again?" This cannot happen, and it is inconceivable.

The commentary on verse 83 of Surah al-Mu'minun (23):

"Indeed, this same talk was said to our forefathers before, just as you say it to us, O Muhammad, but we have never seen any truth in it. This is nothing but the fabrications of the ancients."

The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 84:

Say, [O Muhammad], "To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?"
They will certainly acknowledge that it belongs to Allah; He is its Creator and its Owner. Say to them: Will you not then take heed, and remember that He is able to resurrect and raise the dead?

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, the "Simplified Tafsir") on Surah 23, verse 86:

Say: "Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?" The Throne, which Allah has made the greatest and highest of the created things?
They will surely say, "It belongs to Allah." Say to them: "Will you not then fear His punishment if you worship other than Him?"

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 88:

Say: Who owns everything, and who holds the treasuries of everything? Who grants protection to whoever seeks his protection? No one can grant protection or defend against someone whom God wills to destroy, and no one can repel the evil that God has decreed, if you know this?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 89:

They will answer: "All of that belongs to Allah." Say to them: How, then, are your minds deluded, and how are you deceived and turned away from the Oneness of Allah and obedience to Him, and from believing in the matter of the Resurrection and the Gathering?
Rather, We have brought these deniers the truth in what We sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with, and indeed they are liars in their associating partners with Allah and in their denial of the Resurrection.

God did not take for Himself a son, and there was not with Him any other deity. For if there were more than one deity, each deity would have gone off with its own creation, and they would have contended with one another as the kings of this world do, and the order of the universe would fall into disorder. Glorified is God, exalted and sanctified above their describing Him as having a partner or a son.
He alone knows what is hidden from His creation and what they witness, so exalted is Allah above the partner they claim.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verses 93–94:

Say, [O Messenger]: "My Lord, if You are going to show me in these polytheists what You have promised them of Your punishment, then do not destroy me along with them. Save me from Your punishment and Your wrath, do not place me among the wrongdoing polytheists, but make me among those with whom You are pleased."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verses 93–94:

Say, [O Messenger]: "My Lord, if You are going to show me in these polytheists what You have promised them of Your punishment, then do not destroy me along with them. Save me from Your punishment and Your wrath, do not place me among the wrongdoing polytheists, but make me among those with whom You are pleased."

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 23, verse 95:**

﴿And indeed, We are able to show you what We promise them of punishment.﴾

This is the commentary on Surah al-Mu'minun (23), verse 96, from the Tafsir al-Muyassar of King Fahd Complex:

When your enemies harm you, O Messenger, by word or deed, do not respond to them with harm. Rather, repel their evil with good conduct from you towards them. We are best aware of what these polytheists describe, of their associating partners with Allah and their denial, and We will repay them for it with the worst of recompense.

Say, O Prophet: "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils, which entice people toward falsehood and corruption and turn them away from the truth, and from their whisperings. And I seek refuge in You, O Lord, from their presence in any of my affairs."

Say, O Prophet: "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils, which entice people toward falsehood and corruption and turn them away from the truth, and from their whisperings. And I seek refuge in You, O Lord, from their presence in any of my affairs."

God, may He be exalted, informs us about the condition of the dying person among the disbelievers, or among those who neglected His command, until, when he is about to die and witnesses what has been prepared for him of punishment, he says: ﴿My Lord, send me back!﴾

Perhaps I can make up for what I neglected of faith and obedience. No, that is not granted to him: he will not be answered in what he asked, nor will he be given respite. It is merely a word he utters, a statement that will not benefit him, and in which he is not truthful. Even if he were returned to the world, he would go back to what he was forbidden. The dead will remain in the barrier and the barzakh (the intermediate state) that lies between this world and the Hereafter until the Day of Resurrection and rising.

On the Day of Resurrection, when the angel assigned to it blows into the Horn, and people are raised from their graves, then there will be no boasting of lineages at that time as they used to boast of them in the world, and no one will ask anyone (about his lineage or his affairs).

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 23, verse 102:

Whoever's good deeds are many and whose scales of deeds are heavy with them at the Reckoning, those are the ones who will succeed and attain Paradise.

Whoever's good deeds are light in the scale, and whose evil deeds outweigh them, the greatest of which is shirk (associating partners with Allah), those are the ones who have lost and ruined their own selves, and they will abide forever in the Fire of Hell.
The fire burns their faces, and they are in it with grim, scowling expressions: their lips are drawn back and their teeth are exposed.
It is said to them: "Were not the verses of the Qur'an recited to you in the world, and did you not deny them?"

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 106:

When the messengers conveyed to them and warned them, they will say on the Day of Resurrection: "Our Lord, our appetites and our desires overcame us, those that were decreed for us in Your prior knowledge, and we were, in our deeds, astray from guidance."
"Our Lord, bring us out of the Fire and return us to the worldly life. Then if we revert to misguidance, indeed we are wrongdoers who deserve punishment."
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to them: "Remain in the Fire, humiliated, and do not speak to Me." At that, their supplication and their hope were cut off.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 109:

Indeed, there was a group of My servants, and they are the believers, who would say: "Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive our sins, have mercy on us, and You are the best of the merciful."
So you busied yourselves with mocking them until you forgot the remembrance of God, and you remained in your denial, while you used to laugh at them in scorn and ridicule.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 111:

Indeed, I have rewarded this group of My believing servants with success by entering Paradise, because of their patience in the face of harm and their obedience to Allah.
The wretched in the Fire will be asked: "How many years did you remain on earth?" and "How much of obedience to God did you waste in it?"
They say, owing to the terror of the situation and the severity of the punishment: "We remained in it a day or part of a day, so ask those who count the months and the days."

He said: "You remained only a little while, had you known it." This is said by way of reproach: had you patiently persisted in obedience to Allah for that brief time, you would have won Paradise, if you had had knowledge of that. This is because the length of their stay in the worldly life is very brief compared with the long duration of their abiding forever in the Fire.

"Did you think, O creatures, that We created you without purpose, with no command or prohibition, no reward or punishment, and that you would not be returned to Us in the Hereafter for reckoning and recompense?"

Exalted is God, the King, the Possessor of all things, who is the Truth; His promise is true, His threat is true, and everything from Him is true. He is holy, far above creating anything in vain or without purpose. There is no god but Him, Lord of the Noble Throne. The Throne of the Most Merciful is described as noble because of its exalted status, and the Throne is the greatest of the created things.

Whoever worships another god alongside Allah, the One, for which he has no proof of its deserving worship, then his recompense for his evil deed is with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, there is no success or salvation for the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 23, verse 118:

Say, O Prophet: "My Lord, overlook sins and show mercy; You are the best of those who show mercy, for You accept the repentance of one who has committed a sin and do not punish him for his sin."
